p: If you're using Byron Place as a base for a day on the coast, it's handy to park up, grab what you need and then head out on foot. The town centre is compact, so getting to the seafront doesn't take long. Bring a bag for any sea glass you collect, a warm layer for the North Sea breeze and comfy shoes for walking on the shingle and cliff paths.

Seaham Marina, at the old harbour, is a lovely place to watch the boats come and go, and the heritage centre beside it is home to the town's restored old lifeboat, the George Elmy. The Durham Heritage Coast stretches north and south of the town, and the clifftop paths offer brilliant walks with big views over the sea. Nose's Point, just south of the harbour, was once covered by colliery workings and has since been reclaimed by grassland and wildlife, a remarkable turnaround.

For history fans, Seaham Hall, where Lord Byron married Annabella Milbanke in 1815, is now a luxury hotel and spa, so you'll only get a glimpse from outside unless you're staying or booking a treatment. If you've got more time, the historic city of Durham with its castle and cathedral is a short drive inland, and Sunderland's seafront at Roker and Seaburn is just up the coast for more seaside fun. Put together, it's easy to turn a quick shopping stop into a full day exploring this stretch of the North East coast.
